intro1.heard: Namaste!  This video introduces tool trays, a smart system to track tools and their calibration  on the factory floor.

intro2.heard: You will see the problem it solves, how to use it step by step, its main features and the benefits for your company.

prob1.heard: In most plants, tools are tracked in a paper register or an Excel sheet.

prob2.heard: Tools go missing and nobody can say who took the torque wrench last Tuesday.

prob3.heard: A tool whose calibration has expired can still be used on a job because nothing stops it.  That is a quality risk.

prob4.heard: Entries are made late or not at all.  And when an auditor asks for proof, someone spends hours searching through files.

prob5.heard: Lost tools are bought again and jobs wait while people search.  All of this costs time and money.

sol1.heard: ToolTrays replaces the register with one simple web app.  It works on a computer at the tool crib and on any phone on the shop floor.

sol2.heard: Every tool gets a QR label and if you like, an RFID tag.  So the app always knows where each tool is, who has it and when it is due back.

sol3.heard: There are four roles.  The admin manages people and settings.  The storekeeper runs the tool crib.

sol4.heard: The technician takes tools for jobs.  And the auditor can see everything but cannot change anything.

use0.heard: Now, let us see how to use it.

login1.heard: This is the sign-in page.  Real users sign in with a passkey, their fingerprint, face or phone pin.  There are no passwords to forget or steal.

login2.heard: This demo also has one-click roles.  We will start as Ravi, the storekeeper.

board1.heard: This is the tool board.  It works like a shadow board on the wall.  Every tool has its own place.

board2.heard: The top line shows how many tools are out, how many are overdue and how many are locked.

board3.heard: A solid card means the tool is in the crib.  A dotted outline means it is out and shows who has it and when it is due back.

board4.heard: Overdue tools are marked in red.  A small square in the corner warns that calibration is due soon or has expired.

board5.heard: With one click, you can see only the tools that need attention.

issue1.heard: To issue a tool, the storekeeper opens it and picks the person.

issue2.heard: then chooses when it should come back and clicks Checkout.

issue3.heard: Done!  The board now shows who has the tool.  The time and the storekeeper's name are saved automatically.

ret1.heard: When a tool comes back, the storekeeper opens it and notes its condition, good, damaged, or needs calibration.

ret2.heard: Here, the ratchet is slipping, so we mark it as damaged and click receive.

ret3.heard: A damage tool is quarantined automatically.  Nobody can take it until it is repaired and checked.

cal1.heard: Now, Calibration.  This stock wrench is past its calibration date, so tool trays has locked it.

cal2.heard: Not only the screen, the server and the database itself refuse to issue it.  There is no way around this rule.

cal3.heard: After the tool is calibrated, the storekeeper records who calibrated it and the certificate number.

cal4.heard: The tool is unlocked at once and the next due date is set automatically.

tools1.heard: The tools page lists every tool.  You can search by tag or name and filter by status or calibration.

tools2.heard: For example, here are the tools whose calibration is due soon so they can be planned in time.

tools3.heard: Adding a new tool takes a few seconds.  Then print its QR label and stick it on the tool.

tech1.heard: Now the technicians view on a phone.  Asha signs in.

tech2.heard: Her screen shows the tools she has and when each one is due back.

tech3.heard: To take a tool, she taps Scan and points the camera at the QR label.  She can also type the tag.

tech4.heard: She chooses when she will return it and taps checkout.  It takes about 10 seconds.

off1.heard: Sometimes there is no network signal on the shop floor.  Tool trace keeps working.

off2.heard: The checkout is saved on the phone.

off3.heard: When the signal returns, it is sent automatically exactly once.  Nothing is lost and nothing is counted twice.

sta1.heard: For even faster work, the Crip can have a smart station, a small RFID reader built on an ESP32 board.

sta2.heard: The admin adds a station here.  Each station gets its own secret key.

sta3.heard: Now watch the board.  Asha taps her ID badge at the station and then taps the tool.

sta4.heard: That's it. No typing at all.  And every open screen updates live at the same moment without refreshing.

sta5.heard: Every message from a station is digitally signed.  A fake or altered message is rejected and recorded.

ins1.heard: Every night, a machine learning model studies all past checkouts.

ins2.heard: For each tool that is out right now, it shows the risk of a late return or a loss with the reasons in plain words.

ins3.heard: It also flags unusual checkouts, for example, a tool taken at a node R or kept for much longer than usual.

ins4.heard: A person reviews each flag and decides.  The model only gives an early warning.  It never blames anyone.

ppl1.heard: The admin manages people.  To add someone, enter their email and role and click Create invite.

ppl2.heard: Share the link or QR code.  They create their passkey and they are in.

ppl3.heard: When someone leaves, one click deactivates them and signs them out on every device.

aud1.heard: Finally, the audit trail.  Every action is recorded who did what and when.

aud2.heard: Each record is sealed with a cryptographic hash of the one before, like links in a chain.

aud3.heard: Click Verify Integrity and tool trace proves that no record was changed or deleted.  Even the database owner cannot quietly rewrite history.

feat1.heard: Here are the key features at a glance.

feat2.heard: A live tool board.  Check out by QR code, RFID badge or from the crib.  A calibration lock.  And offline mode.

feat3.heard: Smart stations  Nightly insights  Pascy sign-in withdrawals  And a tamper-proof audit trail

adv0.heard: So, how is this better than a register or an excel sheet?

adv1.heard: With a register, you know where a tool is only if someone wrote it down.  With tool trace, you know in real time.

adv2.heard: A register cannot stop an expired tool from being used.  Tool trace blocks it.

adv3.heard: A register can be changed or lost.  In Tool Trace, any change to a record is detected.

adv4.heard: and a register only tells you the past.  Tool trace warns you early before a tool goes late or missing.

ben0.heard: Now, the key benefits for the company.

ben1.heard: 1. Fewer lost tools and less money spent on replacing them.

ben2.heard: 2. Better Quality  Only calibrated tools reach the job, which supports quality standards and customer audits.

ben3.heard: 3. Time saved.  Issuing a tool takes seconds and audit evidence is ready in minutes, not days.

ben4.heard: 4. Clear accountability.  At every moment, each tool has one named person responsible for it.

ben5.heard: 5. Better Decisions  Usage data shows which tools are in demand and which are rarely used to plan purchases wisely.

ben6.heard: 6. Strong Security  No passwords to steal, access based on roles, and records that cannot be faked.

ben7.heard: And 7. Low cost.  It runs in a browser on the computers and phones you already have and the stations use low cost parts.

start2.heard: Step 1, add your tools and stick on the QR labels.  Step 2, invite your team.

start3.heard: Step 3, Start with one tool crib as a pilot.  Then, roll it out to the other areas of the plant.

end1.heard: Thank you for watching.  Try the live demo yourself at  tooltrace-vigandh.vercel.app  Pick a role and explore.
